text:
The evidence can't say whether the 2021 loss was illegal. It shows that tree cover was lost, but not why, who did it, or whether it was authorized.

What it does show:
- Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021, or 2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha asset.
- The result is corroborated. The JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area, and later years through 2025 were observed.
- Most of the loss (68.1 ha) was in mapped planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). None was in native forest, and 13.2 ha fell outside mapped forest.
- Another 37.3 ha was lost in patches under 0.5 ha, which are not counted as an event.

Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation. So this doesn't show deforestation or land-use change, and it gives no cause, such as harvest, fire, storm or clearing. It also supports no compliance finding.

Legality would need other evidence, such as harvest permits or authorizations, and records of who carried out the work.
